verdict.rationale: Elicit's own docs say it highlights the source of generated content within the relevant papers and quotes tables it draws from. A hands-on user reported getting concepts with citations and links to papers, and another noted that Elicit quotes sources directly. That quoting let them catch a claim contradicted by its own quote, which shows verification works rather than disputing that citations exist. Missing for 10: evidence that every substantive claim (not just column answers and summaries) carries a citation, in-depth documentation of the citation/highlighting UX across Research Agent and reports, and corroboration that cited sources consistently support the claims made.

support.subject: As a researcher, I can see citations for every substantive claim so I can verify it against the underlying source

citations.quote: We then highlight the source of the content within the relevant papers.
If Elicit uses information from a table, it will quote the table
they had a list of concepts with citations and links to papers
